text:
**Short answer:** Pick a power station with at least 1,800 W of continuous AC output. Wattage matters more than battery size here. An induction plate draws up to 1,800 W, and a station with a smaller inverter will shut off or won't run it at all ([Home Power Facts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/induction-cooktop/)).

**My pick: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (about $899).**
- Its 2,600 W inverter handles an 1,800 W plate with headroom. It has 2,073.6 Wh of LiFePO4 battery, and the retailer listed it in stock on 2026-11-04 ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop)).
- Boiling a litre takes only about 90–110 Wh, so a kettle or a few meals won't drain it quickly (same source).
- You can [buy it here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). Dealectric says the link pre-applies a code that saves $44.95.
- Dealectric sells this unit, so the recommendation comes from a seller. The specs fit the requirement, but I only found this one model priced in the results.

**Runtime:**
- On high, a single burner averages about 1,080 W as it cycles. That works out to roughly 45–50 minutes on a 1,000 Wh unit and about 1.5 hours on a 2,000 Wh unit ([BlackoutWise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/induction-cooktop)).
- A steady 1,800 W gives about an hour from a 2,000 Wh station ([PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/devices/induction-cooktop)).
- You can stretch the battery by bringing food to temperature on high, then dropping to 400–800 W to simmer. A 20-minute meal at mixed power levels typically uses 300–500 Wh (same source).

**What won't work:**
- Small stations with 300–600 W inverters can't run it. That includes the EcoFlow RIVER 3, RIVER 3 Plus, BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 and Jackery Explorer 300 v2 ([BlackoutWise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/induction-cooktop), [Home Power Facts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/induction-cooktop/)).
- The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 stops at 1,500 W, so it only works at lower burner settings (BlackoutWise).
- The Goal Zero Yeti 500 puts out 500 W, which is too little (BlackoutWise).
- The smallest unit Home Power Facts found that can run a single burner is the DJI Power 1000, but it lasts only about 0.4 hours at full power.

**Electric kettle:** I didn't find kettle-specific wattage in these results. Most kettles draw less than an 1,800 W induction plate, so a station that handles induction should handle a kettle. That's my inference, not something the sources state.

**Practical tip:** Running near the inverter limit makes the station hot and can trigger thermal shutoff. Keep its vents clear and away from the cooktop's exhaust ([VanLifeKitchens](https://vanlifekitchens.com/guides/can-a-power-station-run-an-induction-cooktop)).
